{{Short description|Categorical treatment of topological spaces}}
{{Other uses|Topological concrete category}}
In [[category theory]], a discipline in [[mathematics]], a '''topological category''' is a category that is [[enriched category|enriched]] over the category of [[compactly generated space|compactly generated]] [[Hausdorff space]]s. They can be used as a foundation for [[higher category theory]], where they can play the role of (<math>\infty</math>,1)-categories. An important example of a topological category in this sense is given by the category of [[CW complex]]es, where each set Hom(''X'',''Y'') of continuous maps from ''X'' to ''Y'' is equipped with the [[compact-open topology]]. {{harv|Lurie|2009}}
